Consult Summary:
- 34-year-old female, four weeks post-C-section, presents with acute onset shortness of breath and recent cough; assessment suggests potential post-operative pulmonary embolism, advised for urgent hospital evaluation.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Shortness of breath started acutely within the past hour while sitting and watching TV.
- Symptom timeline: 
  - Shortness of breath: began 1 hour prior to consultation, no prior similar episodes.
  - New cough: began 1 day prior, non-productive.
  - Soreness in chest on deep inspiration and at C-section scar, both described as tender.
- Past history of frequent coughs and colds, last “a good few months ago.”
- Reports increased awareness of “heart going” (palpitations); no chest pain associated with shortness of breath.
- Denies chest pain at rest; reports chest is “sore” with deep breath (and C-section scar also tender).
- No reported fever, calf pain, or leg swelling. No symptoms in the baby.
- No clear exacerbating or relieving factors mentioned.
- No recent medication except codeine (stopped 1 week ago); no mention of hormonal contraception or immobilization.
- No other associated symptoms discussed.
- Systems review otherwise non-contributory (no other system symptoms elicited).

Past Medical History:
- C-section, 4 weeks ago; no complications during healing reported.
- No additional chronic medical problems mentioned.

Medications:
- Codeine (dose/route/frequency not documented); taken fairly regularly post-operatively, stopped approximately 1 week ago.
- No current regular medications.
- Allergy: Ibuprofen (reaction not specified; patient unable to recall specific type of reaction).

Social History:
- Lives with partner (currently at work).
- Has a newborn baby (baby well, no illness reported).
- No mention of tobacco, alcohol, or recreational drug use.
- No financial or other relevant lifestyle details provided.

Family History:
- Mother has history of clots in legs.

Physical Examination:
- Heart rate: Patient counted 30 beats in unspecified time frame (appeared fast per physician’s assessment, but specific rate or duration not documented).
- No other examination findings or documented vital signs.

Investigations:
- No investigations or test results performed or documented in transcript.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute shortness of breath, new cough, and recent C-section (4 weeks postpartum) in context of possible pulmonary embolism (PE)
  - Assessment: Clinical suspicion for PE given recent C-section, acute onset dyspnea at rest, mild tachycardia, family history of clots, chest soreness.
  - Plan:
    - Advise urgent hospital evaluation for further assessment (possible pulmonary embolism).
    - Advised not to take further codeine until reviewed.
    - Patient to bring baby and necessary items to hospital; no ambulance arranged per patient’s preference.
    - Explained risks (post-operative clots) and need for possible treatment if clot confirmed.
- General Plan:
    - Patient advised to seek immediate care independently.
    - Offered opportunity for questions; none raised.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing elements: 
  - No clear documentation of full review of systems (e.g., leg swelling, fever, hemoptysis, syncope).
  - No objective measurement of vital signs (e.g., exact heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation).
  - No dose/frequency for codeine.
  - No complete allergy details (nature of ibuprofen reaction unspecified).
  - No medication reconciliation or list of all medications.
  - No smoking or alcohol history.
● No internal conflicts detected.
● Transcript quality: Good; clinician-patient exchanges clear; limited by patient’s information and absence of in-person examination.
